<description>
`m_blocks_unlinked` serves two purposes:
 1. finding blocks to `setBlockIndexCandidates` once their parents are
       received
 2. setting `m_chain_tx_count` once the parents are received

In case the parent block of a previously pruned block is received,  2. is currently not being done, because pruning removed the entries from `m_blocks_unlinked`.
This can result in `CheckBlockIndex` failures (#31512, #36021) and incorrect rpc results, plus we are in a temporarily inconsistent state (`m_chain_tx_count` is currently not set, but would get set if we restarted).

This scenario is unlikely to happen during normal node operation unless there are huge reorgs, but it can happen, for example, in `getblockfrompeer` scenarios.
Fix this by leaving pruned blocks in `m_blocks_unlinked` that don't have `m_chain_tx_count` set, and also adding them on restart.

This was one of two reasons, the fuzz target `block_index_tree` couldn't cover pruning of blocks not in the main chain.

The other one is similar to #34521 and #35070 - if we receive a block a second time (after pruning), we could change `nSequenceId` while the block is in `setBlockIndexCandidates` - fix this by attempting to remove it from the set before re-adding it.

After the two issues are fixed, the restriction from `block_index_tree` fuzz target is removed.

Fixes #36021
Fixes #31512
</description>

[40a31d9](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/40a31d97ab118cb030af7d560aedbade3ae4cd36) to [532ffaa](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/532ffaa26d0557c149d7efee544f163fdcf84006):
In addition to addressing review comments, I changed the approach of the first commit, taking some things of a branch from @l0rinc (thanks, added you as coauthor).

In the previous PR branch, pruning never removed anything from `m_blocks_unlinked`. Now, a pruned block is only kept there if it doesn't have its `m_chain_tx_count` yet, i.e. if it is still waiting for an ancestor's transactions. Blocks that are already linked are removed on pruning, as on master. Also, blocks without data are no longer added to setBlockIndexCandidates when they get linked.

The approaches are very similar, the main functional difference is for the (admittedly far-fetched) case that a block is pruned, downloaded again (e.g. via getblockfrompeer) and then pruned again. Another advantage is that we can now have slightly stricter checks in `CheckBlockIndex()`.
</new_statements>
